snippet.text: A verifier that wants to correct its own reason at the same verdict cannot. It can only send a stronger verdict. Nothing is stronger than confirmed, so a confirmed lowering cannot be withdrawn by the verifier: a later confirmed report that holds the claim at the lens's severity is refused, and the claim stays one step down. Under the old rule that later report won, and the claim went back up. The maintainer accepted this cost on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session ("A, and read"), since the lowering still needs evidence at the head and passes the fence. A refused report is an error the verifier reads, and a verifier that never sends an accepted report leaves its claim unjudged, so the review reads not reviewed, as it does today for any claim the verifier skips.

2. A sameness answer of `different`, from any report of the claim, wins over `same`, so an answer may move from same to different and never back. A later report at an equal or weaker verdict that answers `different` where the stored report did not is taken for that answer alone, and the tool says so; the rest of the first report stands. A stronger report that answers `same` where a stored report answered `different` keeps `different`. The maintainer ruled this on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session ("A"), on the round's finding that a first `same` could not be taken back.

The actor matters here: the whole cost being described is what the verifier can no longer do. A second instance of the same shape is on line 12, "a first `same` could not be taken back", which leaves the verifier out altogether.
explanation.whatToDo: Make the verifier the subject. For example: "Nothing is stronger than confirmed, so the verifier cannot withdraw a confirmed lowering." On line 12: "on the round's finding that the verifier could not take back a first `same`."
explanation.whyHere: AGENTS.md, Writing rules, says: "Use active verbs and name who did what. Passive voice only when the actor does not matter." A decision file is something an author reads, so the rule applies to it. This paragraph is the one place the decision states its cost, and the verifier is the actor that cost falls on.

properties.failureScenario: A reader checks the decision against the writing rule in AGENTS.md. Line 34 has \"a confirmed lowering cannot be withdrawn by the verifier\", where the rule wants \"the verifier cannot withdraw a confirmed lowering\". The actor is in the sentence, but as the object of a by-phrase rather than as the subject. That is the form the rule allows only when the actor does not matter, and here the verifier's lost ability is the whole point of the paragraph. Line 12 has the same shape and leaves the actor out entirely. A contributor who copies this decision as a template carries the passive form into later decision files.

# A claim's first report stands unless a stronger verdict follows

Status: agreed by the maintainer on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session ("agree to both changes"), for [issue #657](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/657). Its rule that `different` wins was ruled by the maintainer on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session ("A").

Amends: [2026-10-13-re-scope-held-for-the-compiler.md](2026-10-13-re-scope-held-for-the-compiler.md), its sections "What survives: conflicting reports" and "Goldens", for the conflicting reports and the lowering refused for want of evidence
Amends: [2026-11-08-restore-verifier-clauses.md](2026-11-08-restore-verifier-clauses.md), the strongest-verdict rule it restores from the verifier task-scope and conflicting-reports decisions
Amends: [2026-11-08-dismissal-carries-to-restatement.md](2026-11-08-dismissal-carries-to-restatement.md), for which of a claim's reports gives the sameness answer that decides inheritance

Choice:

1. `report_verdict` refuses a second report of a claim unless its verdict is stronger than the stored one. A replay of the stored report is taken. Otherwise the first report stands: its reason, its evidence, its sameness answers and its lowering. A stronger later verdict still replaces the first report, its lowering included, as before. The refusal says which verdict is stored and any lowering it holds.
2. A sameness answer of `different`, from any report of the claim, wins over `same`, so an answer may move from same to different and never back. A later report at an equal or weaker verdict that answers `different` where the stored report did not is taken for that answer alone, and the tool says so; the rest of the first report stands. A stronger report that answers `same` where a stored report answered `different` keeps `different`. The maintainer ruled this on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session ("A"), on the round's finding that a first `same` could not be taken back.
